The npm wrapper @openai/codex@0.157.1 (4,904 bytes, sha256 813e2a944f4474b7e1826d9ce8bf696ad8d80c68f43f7a7067beec51fa8f5b73) and its platform package @openai/codex@0.157.1-linux-x64 (150,336,017 bytes, sha256 7f12677740f439fe4884c7031d9d703e571cecf5ea9fa3a05abd1bbccc2162a8) matched npm dist.integrity; `npm audit signatures` verified both registry signatures and both attestations, whose SLSA provenance names .github/workflows/rust-release.yml at refs/tags/rust-v0.157.1, commit 36650394c5b38c2990ccf2a3457165ca3e9d9726; and the native binary in the platform package (sha256 3e2584f3...) is byte-identical to the one in the GitHub release asset codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz, whose sha256 equals the API digest. The verified wrapper was installed into a new tools/codex-0.157.1 prefix whose files are byte-identical to both tarballs. In a bwrap sandbox with a private loopback-only network, a read-only root and a fresh scratch CODEX_HOME per case (no credential read, ~/.codex untouched), `codex --version` printed codex-cli 0.157.1 (baseline: 0.155.1), `codex exec --help` was byte-identical between the versions and `codex --help` differed only by the new --no-daemon flag. Against a loopback fake Responses provider set only through -c overrides, the landscape-sweep lane's argv (top-level --search, then exec --ignore-user-config --skip-git-repo-check -s read-only -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort="max" --output-schema -o --json, stdin /dev/null) behaved the same on both versions: a success turn emitted thread.started, turn.started, item.completed and turn.completed with usage input 11, cached 3, output 7 and reasoning 2, wrote the -o file, and sent reasoning effort max and a json_schema text format equal to the --output-schema file; a 429 usage_limit_reached answer ended with exit 1 and an error event plus a turn.failed event whose message says 'You’ve hit your usage limit. Try again later.', which the sweep's limit rule detects. With the fake provider marked as supporting standalone web search, `codex --search exec` sent external_web_access false to the search endpoint on both versions, the same as no flag, and only `codex exec -c web_search="live"` sent true; 0.157.1 reported the literal-URL open as action open_page with results, where 0.155.1 reported it as other without results. A scratch CODEX_HOME that 0.157.1 had migrated (state_5.sqlite 55 to 57 migrations, thread_history_1.sqlite 6 to 7) still served a 0.155.1 exec turn. At the two tags, the exec --json event schema differs only by an optional web_search `results` field and exec/src/cli.rs is identical.
limitations: Not independently reviewed: the qualification, the switch and this receipt come from one worker session (Claude Opus 5.5); the refresh coordinator owns the independent-review round, and no cross-family review ran.

Staged, not switched, and no live model call ran on 0.157.1: a live call would either copy the ChatGPT credential into an isolated CODEX_HOME (not allowed; docs/secret-storage.md) or run the newer binary against the shared ~/.codex while the sweep runs 0.155.1. GPT-6 turns through 0.157.1 are unmeasured until the coordinator's post-switch probe (results.json switch_commands_for_the_coordinator).

The fake provider is a stand-in. It exercises request construction, SSE parsing, event emission, -o, the 429 mapping and the web-search extension's settings; it does not exercise the OpenAI provider, ChatGPT authentication, the real usage-limit payload (which named a reset time on 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-26), streamed deltas, reasoning items, sandboxed tool execution, compaction or long multi-turn sessions.

The --search result was measured with a custom provider marked supports_standalone_web_search. That the OpenAI provider behaves the same rests on source reading (the same web-search extension and mode resolution; stage/source-checks.txt), not on a live measurement, and exec --json does not expose the effective mode (openai/codex issue #35415, open). It is a pre-existing 0.155.1 behaviour, not a regression.
The count of 32 openPage and 6 search actions in the sweep lane gpt6-discover-workers comes from that lane's private local Codex session file, read for action counts only and not published.

The rollback state probe is one exec turn in a scratch home. The TUI, resume, the background server that 0.157.0 starts automatically for eligible interactive sessions, and the Codex desktop app were not tried against a migrated ~/.codex.

No pin moves: adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json, adoption/pins-macos-arm64.json and manifests/stack.json keep codex 0.155.1, and catalogs/landscape/foundation.json keeps the native-clients and agent-sdks winner pins at 0.155.1; this receipt is unbound until a switch and a verdict wave. catalogs/landscape/upstream-snapshot.json now lists codex in newer_stable_release_review_queue.

Upstream tests (cargo test) were not run on this host, and both tags are unsigned. The rust-v0.157.1 release body says its highlights could not be generated; its five commits after rust-v0.157.0 were read from the compare API (all Windows console and daemon-launch fixes).
Linux x86_64 only, one host; nothing here is macOS evidence.
